payload.public_summary: The only blocking ambiguity was converted into a simplest-first refinement path. There are no remaining problem-class questions, so the intake is scientifically executable and candidate-ready.

specification_sections.name: purpose
specification_sections.content: Derive the optical absorption coefficient alpha as a function of photon energy hbar omega for a direct-gap semiconductor from single-particle Bloch states in the independent-particle approximation.

specification_sections.name: scientific_target
specification_sections.content: Produce a derivation tree for direct-gap interband absorption and a closed-form alpha(hbar omega), handled in a simplest-first refinement path from edge scaling to the full symbolic prefactor.

specification_sections.name: givens_and_starting_point
specification_sections.content: Start from single-particle Bloch valence and conduction states. Use Fermi's golden rule for vertical interband transitions in a direct-gap semiconductor. Use a parabolic two-band model with conduction and valence bands, reduced mass mu, band gap Eg, and a constant interband momentum matrix element.

specification_sections.name: notation_and_conventions
specification_sections.content: Use SI units. Use Eg and mu as symbols. Assume unpolarized light and isotropic bands, so the absorption is treated as a scalar alpha(hbar omega).

specification_sections.name: assumptions_and_regime
specification_sections.content: Include vertical interband transitions, independent particles, parabolic two-band dispersion, constant momentum matrix element, zero-temperature occupations, the joint density of states, and a delta-function line shape. Exclude excitons, local-field and Coulomb-enhancement effects, phonon-assisted or indirect processes, free-carrier absorption, k dot p warping beyond the parabolic edge, finite lifetime or broadening, finite temperature, and many-body self-energy effects.

specification_sections.name: scope_and_non_goals
specification_sections.content: No numerics, no code, and no materials-specific DFT. The result is an analytic textbook derivation, not a material-calibrated prediction.

specification_sections.name: required_output
specification_sections.content: Provide the derivation tree and a simplest-first ladder in which rung 0 gives the near-edge functional form of alpha(hbar omega) up to an overall constant, and the final rung upgrades that result to the full closed-form symbolic prefactor retaining the constant momentum-matrix-element normalization.

specification_sections.name: validation_criteria
specification_sections.content: The derivation must stay within the independent-particle direct-gap vertical-transition model, preserve the stated included and excluded physics, use SI conventions, and culminate in a full symbolic alpha(hbar omega) expression after the simplest-first upgrade path.

specification_sections.name: agent_discretion
specification_sections.content: All remaining non-blocking presentation and convention choices are owned by the derivation agent and should follow standard textbook defaults consistent with the user's simplest-first policy.

declared_defaults.title: Unit system
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly fixed SI units.

declared_defaults.title: Matrix-element representation
declared_defaults.statement: Use the momentum-matrix-element form for the interband optical coupling.
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly specified a constant momentum matrix element, making this the direct textbook convention.

declared_defaults.title: Gauge handling
declared_defaults.statement: Use the standard long-wavelength optical coupling convention consistent with the momentum-matrix-element formulation, without treating gauge choice as a separate branch.
declared_defaults.rationale: Gauge is a convention, not a blocking physics decision, and the user requested textbook defaults for unspecified items.
alternatives: Velocity gauge treated explicitly as the primary presentation

declared_defaults.title: Line shape
declared_defaults.statement: Use an ideal delta-function line shape with no phenomenological broadening.
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly excluded finite lifetime and broadening.

declared_defaults.title: Route to alpha
declared_defaults.statement: Use the most direct textbook route from the interband transition rate to alpha, introducing equivalent response-function relations only when algebraically useful.
declared_defaults.rationale: The deliverable is alpha(hbar omega) itself, so this avoids unnecessary convention branches.
alternatives: Route via imaginary dielectric function epsilon_2
Route via optical conductivity then conversion to alpha

declared_defaults.title: Real-part treatment
declared_defaults.statement: Do not derive a separate real part of the dielectric function unless needed for an intermediate consistency relation.
declared_defaults.rationale: The requested observable is alpha(hbar omega), not the full complex dielectric function.
alternatives: Kramers-Kronig reconstruction of the real part
External model for the real part of epsilon

declared_defaults.title: Band model
declared_defaults.statement: Use the parabolic two-band conduction-plus-valence model near the direct gap edge.
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly fixed this model and excluded higher-order warping.

declared_defaults.title: Matrix-element k dependence
declared_defaults.statement: Treat the interband momentum matrix element as k independent.
declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly fixed a constant momentum matrix element.

refinement_ladder.name: Edge-scaling baseline
refinement_ladder.relaxes: Nothing; this is the textbook-simplest baseline compatible with the fixed physics, keeping only the near-edge functional dependence of alpha(hbar omega) up to an overall constant.

refinement_ladder.name: Full symbolic prefactor
refinement_ladder.relaxes: Relaxes the omission of the overall multiplicative constant at rung 0 by carrying the constant momentum-matrix-element prefactor and equivalent optical normalization factors explicitly.
